properties.statement_tex:
Let $G$ be a connected loopless graph on $n\ge2$ vertices, let $B$ be an oriented
edge-by-vertex incidence matrix, and let $C=\operatorname{diag}(c_e)$ with
$c_e>0$. If $Q$ is the Euclidean orthogonal projection onto
$\operatorname{im}(C^{1/2}B)$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:localization}
  \bigl\|\,|Q|\,\bigr\|_{2\to2}\le 2\log n.
\end{equation}

properties.statement_tex:
For every strictly positive probability vector $\lambda$ on $E$, there
is a probability vector $\sigma$ with $\sigma_e\ge\lambda_e/2$ such
that the orthogonal projection $P$ onto $V$ in $\ell_2(\sigma)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:projection-row-sums}
 \max_{e\in E}\sum_{f\in E}|P_{ef}|\le H.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\|P\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le H$, and both $P$ and
$I-P$ are contractions on $\ell_2(\sigma)$.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $h$ be a bounded real function supported on a region of finite
$\nu$-measure, and let $S$ be its signed Poisson sum.
For $q>2$ and $\epsilon>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:poisson-moments}
 \int|h|^q\,d\nu
 \le\E|S|^q
 \le(1+\epsilon)\int|h|^q\,d\nu
   +C_{q,\epsilon}\left(\int h^2\,d\nu\right)^{q/2}.
\end{equation}

properties.statement_tex:
Fix nonnegative integers $g,k,w,a$, and interpret
$\mathrm{AE}(g,(k,w),a)$ exactly as the almost-embeddable family of
Lee and Sidiropoulos~\cite[Theorem~1.7]{LS09}. Let
$h_0=h_0(g,k,w,a)\in\N_0$ be the target treewidth bound and let
$D=D(g,k,w,a)\ge1$ be a finite stochastic distortion bound supplied there.
Put
\[
 \widehat h=\max\{h_0,1\},\qquad
 K(g,k,w,a)=D\max\{C_{\mathrm{pl}},C_{\widehat h+1}\},
\]
where $C_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the constant of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, and
$C_t$ is the companion's constant for bags of cardinality at most
$t\ge2$. Every finite connected simple graph $G$ in this named family,
with strictly positive real edge lengths, admits a map $f$ into a real
$L_1$ space satisfying
\[
 d_G(u,v)\le\|f(u)-f(v)\|_1
 \le K(g,k,w,a)d_G(u,v)\qquad(u,v\in V(G)).
\]
For the same underlying graph, $K(g,k,w,a)$ also bounds the undirected
fractional concurrent flow--cut gap $\phi_*/\lambda_*$ for the finite
nonnegative capacities and demands defined in Section~\ref{intro:flow},
whenever $\lambda_*>0$.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $0<\zeta<1$, let $E>0$, and set
\begin{equation}\label{int:constants}
 \begin{gathered}
 \delta=E/8,\qquad a_0=10^{-6}\zeta\delta,\qquad
 q=\zeta\delta/20,\\
 \rho_0=\zeta\delta/1000,\qquad
 M=\lceil15/\zeta\rceil+3,\qquad N=6(M+1).
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Suppose $0<a\le a_0$, and let $p:Y\to\R$ be
$(1-\zeta)$-Lipschitz for $d_J$.  There is a random function
$Q:Y\to\R$, obtained using finitely many independent scalar noises
uniform on $[q,2q]$, with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every realization, $Q$ respects all switches, is
$1$-Lipschitz for $d_J$, and satisfies $|Q(v)-p(v)|\le6\delta<E$.
\item Its pieces use finitely many named atoms of the form
\begin{equation}\label{int:atom-form}
 A(v)=C+\varepsilon d_J(k,v),\qquad \varepsilon\in\{-1,1\},\quad k\in Y.
\end{equation}
Each name specifies a source $k$ and sign $\varepsilon$ fixed before the
noises are sampled; the intercept $C$ is random. Whenever the construction
reuses an atom, it retains its name.
\item For a fixed $x\in Y$ and $0<\rho\le\rho_0$, there is a list
$\mathcal A(x,\rho)$ of at most $N$ atom names and sources, determined
without the noises, that contains the name of every atom selected by $Q$ on
$B_{d_J}(x,\rho)$.  Except on an event of probability at most
\begin{equation}\label{int:probability}
 \frac{N^2}{q}(8\rho+\eta),
\end{equation}
one named atom is selected throughout this ball.
\end{enumerate}
Here $\eta=0$ for continuous uniform noises.  Alternatively, each noise
may be uniform on an equally spaced grid including both endpoints of
$[q,2q]$, and $\eta$ in \eqref{int:probability} may be the largest grid
spacing.  The same conclusions hold for any set of points reached
from $x$ by band paths of length at most $\rho$, including the points
and representatives encountered on those paths.

properties.statement_tex:
Condition on arbitrary prior data. Let $W$ be the union of a nonempty
family of band paths issuing from a fixed point $x$, each of length at
most $\rho$. The set $W$ and these paths are fixed by the prior data.
Suppose that $Q_1,\ldots,Q_s$ are interpolation constructions, each
on a band component containing all these paths. Their geometries,
inputs, and portals are fixed by the prior data, and their fresh noise
families are mutually independent. The bands and their intrinsic metrics
may differ; each of the specified paths must be permitted in every band.
Denote the constants of $Q_i$ in \eqref{int:constants} by
$q_i,N_i,\rho_{0,i}$.

Allow inputs $c_i+\varepsilon_iQ_i$, with
$\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and $c_i$ fixed by the prior data.
Also allow one fixed branch $f$ and $t$ branches $g_j+\beta_j$,
where $f$ and the $g_j$ are fixed functions whose restrictions to each
specified path, parametrized by arclength, are $L$-Lipschitz. The
$\beta_j$ are fresh independent uniform noises on intervals of length
$w_j>0$, independent also of the interpolation noises. All functions respect the switches used by the paths.
Set
\[
 L_* =\max(1,L),\qquad
 S=1+t+\sum_{i=1}^sN_i,\qquad
 q_* =\min\bigl(\{q_i:1\le i\le s\}\cup
                         \{w_j:1\le j\le t\}\bigr).
\]
Assume that there is at least one randomized input and that
$\rho\le\min_i\rho_{0,i}$ when $s>0$. Any fixed expression formed
from these inputs by finitely many minima and maxima selects one
branch and, for a selected interpolation, one atom throughout $W$,
except with conditional probability at most
\begin{equation}\label{int:comparison-probability}
 \frac{S^2}{q_*}(8L_*\rho+\eta).
\end{equation}
Continuous noises have $\eta=0$; for equally spaced endpoint grids
$\eta$ can be the largest spacing of any noise used here. The
expression uses each interpolation with a single chosen sign and
shift; repeated appearances of that same input are given the same
name.

Suppose a system of sets is nested increasingly on each column, respects
switches, and has symmetric-difference measure at most vertical length.
It defines an $L_1$ pseudometric dominated by $d$. It also admits the
following refinement with the same upper bound.

For a label $\omega$, join two columns when one of their switches occurs
at a height active for $\omega$. To an active point assign the unit vector
indexed by its component in this finite graph, and to an inactive point
assign zero. Integrating the $\ell_1$ distances of these vectors gives the
refined pseudometric. It dominates the original symmetric-difference
pseudometric.

If a non-neighbor link has inactive tip and two active points have
representatives strictly on opposite sides of it, their refined distance
for that label is $2$.

For every integer $k\ge2$ there is a finite constant $C_k\ge1$ with the
following property. If a finite connected graph $G=(V,E)$ admits a tree
decomposition with bags of size at most $k$, then, for every edge-length

decomposition, and all ratios of edge lengths.

properties.statement_tex:
The following statements hold for a tree decomposition of a connected graph.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item If a bag $B$ lies on the tree path between bags $A$ and $C$, every
 graph path from a vertex of $A$ to a vertex of $C$ meets $B$.
 \item For adjacent bags $A,C$, their intersection separates the unions
 of bags on the two sides of the corresponding tree edge. In particular,
 adjacent nonempty bags have nonempty intersection.
 \item If $A_0,\ldots,A_r$ occur in this order on a tree path and

properties.statement_tex:
Suppose a finite schedule requires at most $q$ simultaneous reserved
pairs in each memory copy, including any temporary reservation made
before another is released.  Updates may be made at the current bag, or
on a child-specific copy at its parent bag before moving to the child.
Before processing the root, updates at the empty interface are also
allowed.  Every update uses a perturbation satisfying the bounds above
and vanishing on its interface.

Choose
\[
 N=2q+k!+2,
 \qquad
 M=\bigl(B(N-1)+2\bigr)\Delta.
\]
Then all requested updates and reservations can be carried out.  They
produce symmetric bag measures $\mu_t$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Each $\mu_t$ has the same total mass $m=2NM$, and neighboring bag
measures have equal traces on their intersection.
\item Every particle height is at distance at least $2\Delta$ from each
endpoint of the sweep interval $[-M,M]$.
\item The pseudometric $D_\mu$ obtained by Markov gluing satisfies
\[
 D_\mu(u,v)\le U\,d(u,v)
 \quad\text{for all }u,v\in V,
 \qquad U=NL(N-1).
\]
\item If a pair is reserved from a launch bag through a later bag on a
descending path, its fixed symmetric two-particle cut measure has trace
dominated by $\mu_t$ at every bag on that segment.  The segment includes
the launch and release bags, even when the particles are reused at the
release bag.  A reservation launched at the empty interface has the same
property from the root onward.
\end{enumerate}
The statements hold for each realization of any auxiliary randomness.
For measurable randomized choices, taking expectations also gives an
$L_1$ pseudometric with the same upper bound.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $A\subseteq V$ be nonempty, put $h(z)=d(z,A)$, and let
$0<\eta<1/4$. One can sample a random function
\[
  g=\xi h+v,
\]
using randomness independent of any previously sampled data. The
function $v$ is constructed by first sampling a finite indexed family
of nonnegative functions $(\varphi_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$ on $V$,
called bumps, and then setting
\[
 v=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}U_i\varphi_i.
\]
Conditional on the bump family, the coefficients
$U_i$ are independent and uniform on $[0,1]$. The following properties
hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\xi$ is uniform on $[1,2]$ and independent of the bump family
      and all its coefficients;
      $v$ is $1$-Lipschitz and satisfies $0\leq v\leq\eta h/2$.
      Consequently $g|_A=0$, $\operatorname{Lip}(g)\leq3$, and
      \[
        h\leq g\leq \tfrac52h\leq\tfrac52\Delta.
      \]
\item Set $c=\alpha/8$ and $\rho=\pi/2$. For each fixed $x$ with
      $D_0=h(x)>0$, there is an event of probability at least $\rho$,
      determined by the bump family, on which an index $i(x)\in\mathcal I$,
      also determined by that family, selects a bump $\varphi_x=\varphi_{i(x)}$ satisfying
      \[
        \varphi_x(x)\geq c\eta D_0,
        \qquad
        \varphi_x(z)=0\quad\text{if }d(x,z)>4\eta D_0.
      \]
      Write $U_x=U_{i(x)}$. Conditional on the bump family, $U_x$ is uniform and independent
      of $\xi$, of the other bump coefficients, and of all previously
      sampled data. In particular,
      $v=v^{\setminus x}+U_x\varphi_x$, where the remaining coefficients
      defining $v^{\setminus x}$ are independent of $U_x$.
\end{enumerate}
Different vertices may select the same bump and coefficient. The
constants in these assertions are independent of $\eta$, $A$, the
number of vertices, and the ratio of the edge lengths. Only finitely many
random partitions and coefficients are required.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $A_0,A_1$ be nonempty finite structures in the same binary relational
vocabulary, and let $K_i\leq\operatorname{Aut}(A_i)$ for $i\in\{0,1\}$.
Let $s,m,M$ be positive integers satisfying
\[
 \max\{4,m+1\}s\leq M.
\]
Assume the following two properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A_0$ and $A_1$ satisfy the same $C^M$ sentences.
\item In each $A_i$, any two tuples of length at most
      $\max\{2,m\}s$ with the same $C^M$ type lie in the same $K_i$ orbit.
\end{enumerate}
For $i\in\{0,1\}$, let $D_i$ consist of the objects $x$ in
$\mathrm{HF}(A_i)$ such that $x$ and every object in its transitive closure
have a $K_i$-support of length at most $s$.  Equip $D_i$ with membership,
an atom predicate, and the relations of $A_i$, interpreted as false on
arguments containing a non-atom.  Then $D_0$ and $D_1$ satisfy the same
$C^m$ sentences.
properties.title: CPT:thm:hf-transfer

with repetition allowed, from $A_0,A_1$.  If $|P|+d\leq M$, then for every
realized type $\rho$ of length $|P|+d$, the numbers of tuples $\gamma$

\[
 \operatorname{tp}_M(P,\gamma)=\rho,

 \operatorname{tp}_M(P',\gamma')=\rho
\]

the other.  Equal types also have equal types on every projected or
reordered subtuple.

properties.statement_tex:
Suppose predicates in a relational formula $T$ are replaced by formulas
whose free variables are among their displayed argument variables and
whose free-variable measure is at most $w$. Capture-avoiding substitution
produces a formula of free-variable measure at most
$\max\{\operatorname{fw}(T),w\}$. This allows repeated arguments and
unused displayed argument variables. Moreover a formula of measure at
most $w$ can be renamed to use at most $w+1$ variable names.

properties.statement_tex:
There exist a vocabulary \(\tau\) of eight binary relations, a fixed polynomial
\(p\), and a \(\CPT+\WSC\) sentence \((\Phi,p)\) with one occurrence of a WSC
operator such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \((\Phi,p)\) has a Boolean value on every finite \(\tau\)-structure;
\item no \(\CPT\) sentence over \(\tau\) has the same true-model class.
\end{enumerate}
The \(\CPT\) sentences in \textup{(ii)} may use counting and hereditarily
finite sets of unrestricted finite rank.

blocks of $A_b$ are nonempty, and
\begin{equation}\label{str:size-formula}
 |A_b|=N_L=
 \sum_{e\in E_L}3^{2|F(e)|+1}
 +\sum_{v\in V_L}3^{2|F(v)|+d(v)-1}.
\end{equation}
Thus $N_L$ is independent of $b$, and
\[
 |Y_e|\le3^9,\qquad |X_v|\le3^{29},\qquad
 L^3\le N_L\le(3^{10}+3^{29})L^3.
\]

group.  Its identity is $(0,0)$ and $(a,k)^{-1}=(-a,-k)$.
The subgroup $\{0\}\times K$, identified with $K$, is central, and
projection onto $C_F$ is a surjective homomorphism with kernel $K$.
With the convention $[h,h']=hh'h^{-1}(h')^{-1}$, one has
\begin{equation}\label{str:commutator}
 [(a,k),(a',k')]
 =\left(0,\sum_{f\in F}\omega(a_f,a'_f)c^f\right).
\end{equation}

properties.statement_tex:
The sentence \((\Phi,p)\) of
Equations~\eqref{sen:sentence} and~\eqref{sen:polynomial} is a fixed
\(\CPT+\WSC\) sentence over \(\tau\). It evaluates to either true or
false on every finite \(\tau\)-structure, never to \(\dagger\), and its
true-model class is isomorphism-invariant.

More explicitly, it is true precisely when \(P\ne\emptyset\) and there
exists \(\alpha\in P\) such that every terminal state of the guarded
selection is complete and extends to consistent configurations as in
Lemma~\ref{sen:tree-test}.

Let $A_b$ be a grid structure, $\alpha\in P$, and $x$ a compatible prefix
of length $j<r$.  For every ordered pair $s,s'\in D(\alpha,x)$ there is
$g\in M(\alpha,x)$ with $g(s)=s'$.  The map $g$ preserves the full input,
fixes every block setwise, and fixes every atom of $x$ individually.
Consequently every selection path for $\alpha$ chooses one atom from
each edge outside $T$, in order, maintains compatibility, and then
stabilizes with the dummy choice.  All its witnessing maps respect
$\alpha$ and the entire preceding history.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $L\ge2$, $b\in\F^{V_L}$, and $N=|A_b|$. Suppose $\mathcal X$ is
a finite $H$-invariant, membership-transitive family of atoms and
hereditarily finite sets over $A_b$, with $|\mathcal X|\le N^q$ for
some $q\ge0$. Every member of $\mathcal X$ and every recursive member
has a $K$-support of length at most $2L(q\log_3N)^2$. In particular,
every member is hereditarily $s$-supported for
\begin{equation}\label{sup:length}
 s=\left\lceil2L(q\log_3N+1)^2\right\rceil+1.
\end{equation}
All the supports may be padded to length exactly $s$. For fixed $q$,
\[
 s=O_q\bigl(L(1+\log L)^2\bigr).
\]

properties.statement_tex:
Let $B_0,B_1$ be nonempty finite structures in the same finite relational
vocabulary of arity at most two, and let
$K_i\leq\Aut(B_i)$ for $i=0,1$.
Let $s,m,M$ be positive integers with
\[
                         \max\{4,m+1\}s\leq M.
\]
Suppose that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B_0$ and $B_1$ satisfy the same $C^M$ sentences;
\item in each $B_i$, any two tuples of length at most
      $\max\{2,m\}s$ having the same $C^M$ type belong to the same
      $K_i$-orbit.
\end{enumerate}
Then $D_s(B_0,K_0)$ and $D_s(B_1,K_1)$ satisfy the same $C^m$ sentences
in membership, atomhood, and the base relations.

properties.statement_tex:
Fix a CPT sentence \(\psi\).  There are an integer \(m\ge1\) and, for
each sufficiently large input size \(n\), a \(C^m\) sentence
\(\widehat\psi_n\) with the following property.

Let \(A\) be an \(n\)-element input and let \(D\subseteq\HF(A)\) be
membership-transitive, contain all atoms and all pure HF sets, and contain
\(\mathcal T_\psi(A)\).  Interpret membership and the atom predicate on
\(D\), and interpret each input relation as false if an argument is a
set.  Then
\[
 D\models\widehat\psi_n
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \psi\text{ evaluates to true on }A.
\]
The formula \(\widehat\psi_n\) depends only on \(\psi\) and \(n\), not on
\(A\) or \(D\).  Its length and counting constants may depend on \(n\);
\(m\) does not.

properties.statement_tex:
There is a uniform deterministic algorithm that, given a prime $p$ in
binary and a nonzero dense polynomial $f\in\Fp[x]$ of degree $n$, outputs
its leading coefficient and its distinct monic irreducible factors with
their multiplicities in
\[
 O\bigl(((n+1)\lceil\log_2p\rceil)^{10^{12}}\bigr)
\]
bit operations, with absolute implied constant. A constant polynomial
returns an empty factor list. The algorithm uses no randomness,
integer-factorization oracle, primitive-root oracle, or GRH assumption.

properties.statement_tex:
There is a uniform deterministic algorithm with the following guarantee.
Its input is a prime $p$ and a nonzero dense polynomial $f\in\Fp[x]$.
If $p>B^{200000}$ and $n\ge2$, its input also includes one auxiliary
prime $\ell_q$ satisfying \eqref{eq:auxiliary} for each prime $q\le n$.
It outputs the complete factorization of $f$, including multiplicities.
Let $E=\max(2,\max_q\ell_q)$, with $E=2$ when no auxiliary primes are
required. For an absolute constant $C$, the algorithm uses
$O((B+E)^C)$ bit operations. It uses neither randomness nor an integer
factorization or primitive-root oracle.

properties.statement_tex:
Suppose the auxiliary primes \eqref{table:primes} are supplied, and
suppose a deterministic procedure has the following uniform contract:
for every integer $1\le b<n$, it factors every monic polynomial of degree at
most $b$ over $\mathbb F_p$ using table entries only for primes at most
$b$.  Then the complete table through $n$ can be built in increasing
prime order.  Its construction calls that procedure at most once for each
odd prime $q\le n$, on a polynomial of degree $q-1$; each such call uses
only already constructed table entries.

Apart from these factorization calls, the construction has bit cost
polynomial in $E$, $n$, and $\log p$, with an absolute exponent.  Each
stored odd-prime field has degree at most $q-1$, and the temporary field
$V_q$ has degree at most $q(q-1)$ over $\mathbb F_p$.

Let $k$ be an explicit finite field of cardinality $Q$ and characteristic $p$.
Let $q$ be an odd prime dividing $Q-1$, let $\zeta\in k$ have order $q$, and
let $\omega\in k$ generate the full $q$-primary subgroup of $k^*$.
Let $H\in k[X]$ be monic and square-free, with $h=\deg H\ge1$, and suppose
$p>h^2$.  Given a unit $a\in k[X]/H$ that is promised to be a $q$-th power,
one can deterministically construct $b$ with $b^q=a$.
The bit cost is polynomial in $q$, $h$, and the length of the given field
representation.  The procedure uses only arithmetic and zero tests over $k$,
and so admits simultaneous execution as in Lemma~\ref{ff:simultaneous}.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $k$ be an explicitly represented finite field of characteristic $p$,
let $q$ be an odd prime, and suppose that a primitive $q$th root of unity
$\zeta\in k$ and a generator of the full $q$-primary subgroup of $k^*$
are given.  Let $F\in k[X]$ be monic and square-free, of positive degree
$N$ divisible by $q$.  Put
\[
 K_0=k(X),\qquad
 \mathcal L=K_0[Y]/(Y^q-F),\qquad \rho(Y)=\zeta Y.
\]
Let $G\in K_0^*$, write $D$ for the maximum of its reduced numerator
and denominator degrees, and assume
\begin{equation}\label{norm:characteristic}
 p>(N+2D+1)^2.
\end{equation}
If $G$ belongs to $\operatorname{Norm}_{\mathcal L/K_0}(\mathcal L^*)$, a deterministic
algorithm constructs $h\in \mathcal L^*$ with
\[
 \prod_{j=0}^{q-1}\rho^j(h)=G.
\]
Its bit complexity, and the degrees of the rational coefficients of
$h$ in the basis $1,Y,\ldots,Y^{q-1}$, are bounded by fixed polynomials
in $q,N,D$, and $\log|k|$.  It uses no polynomial factorization oracle.
Its field-dependent branches use only zero tests, so the algorithm
admits the simultaneous execution of Lemma~\ref{ff:simultaneous}.
properties.title: Promised norm solver

On the curve $C$ above, the following operations are deterministic and use
a number of field operations polynomial in $q,N$, the degrees occurring in
the input representation, the absolute degrees of the divisors
materialized during the operation, and the parameter $\ell$ in the third
operation:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item divisor addition, negation, coefficientwise minimum and maximum,
 and the action of $\sigma$;
 \item construction of the divisor of an explicitly represented nonzero
 function, and evaluation of its valuation and leading coefficient at a
 specified ramification point or point at infinity;
 \item computation of the Riemann--Roch space
 $L(D+\ell\infty_0)$ for $\ell\geq 0$;
 \item replacement of a degree-zero divisor $D$ by a linearly equivalent
 divisor $D'$ satisfying $\|D'\|\leq 2g$, with a function $a$ such that
 $D'=D+\operatorname{div}(a)$.
\end{enumerate}
These algorithms do not require factorization of the polynomials defining
the finite supports.  Their decisions use only field zero tests, so they
admit simultaneous execution as in Lemma~\ref{ff:simultaneous}.

\[
 \deg h^+=\sum_{P\text{ finite}}\max(v_P(D),0)[k(P):k],\qquad
 \deg h^-=\sum_{P\text{ finite}}\max(-v_P(D),0)[k(P):k].
\]
The polynomial $H=h^+h^-$ satisfies~\eqref{div:bound}.  If $\deg D=0$ and
$j=h^+/h^-$, then
\begin{equation}\label{div:orbitnorm}
 \operatorname{div}_C(j)=\sum_{a=0}^{q-1}\sigma^aD.
\end{equation}

\begin{equation}

\label{geom:sum-epsilon}
\end{equation}
More explicitly, let $D$ be a geometric degree-zero divisor, let
$W\in\Lambda$, and suppose that
\[
                  \operatorname{div}(h)=(1-\sigma)D-W.
\]
Then $\operatorname{Norm}_{\overline K(C)/\overline K(X)}(h)$ is a
nonzero constant.  Choose $\gamma\in\overline K^*$ with
\[

\]
Then $h(P_i)$ is defined and nonzero, and the residues
\begin{equation}
 l_i=v_{P_i}(D)-\log_\zeta\bigl(h(P_i)/\gamma\bigr)
                   \quad\text{in }\mathbb F_q
\label{geom:labels}
\end{equation}
satisfy
\begin{equation}
                         ([D],W)=\sum_{i=1}^N l_i\epsilon_i
                         \quad\text{in }T_1.
\label{geom:label-expansion}
\end{equation}
Here $v_{P_i}(D)$ is the coefficient of $P_i$ in $D$, and
$\log_\zeta$ is the unique exponent modulo $q$ of a $q$-th root of unity.

For $1\le t\le m$, set
\begin{equation}
           d_t=\lambda^{m-t}d_m,\qquad
           W_t=\lambda^{-(t-1)}Ne\in\Lambda,
\label{geom:separation-data}
\end{equation}
and choose any degree-zero divisor $D_t$ over $k$ representing $d_t$.
The lattice divisions defining $W_t$ exist and are unique.

Starting at $t=1$, make the following test, advancing to $t+1$ only when
all labels at $t$ agree.  Choose $h_t\in k(C)^*$ and $\gamma_t\in k^*$
such that
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{div}(h_t)=(1-\sigma)D_t-W_t,
       \qquad \gamma_t^q=\operatorname{Norm}(h_t),
\label{geom:separation-functions}
\end{equation}
and form the labels
\begin{equation}
            l_{i,t}=v_{P_i}(D_t)
               -\log_\zeta\bigl(h_t(P_i)/\gamma_t\bigr)
                    \quad\text{in }\mathbb F_q.
\label{geom:separation-labels}
\end{equation}
At every reached test these choices exist over $k$ and the labels are
defined.  For some reached $t\le m$, the labels are not all equal.
This conclusion holds for every choice of the representatives $D_t$ and
of the functions and roots in~\eqref{geom:separation-functions}.

Let $p$ be prime, $L=\lceil\log_2p\rceil$, and
$B=20+(n+1)(L+1)$.  Suppose that $p>B^{200000}$ and that
$F\in\mathbb F_p[X]$ is monic, square-free, totally split, and of odd
degree $3\le N\le n$.  Choose an odd prime $q\mid N$.
Suppose that the following data are supplied explicitly:
\begin{itemize}
\item a field $K/\mathbb F_p$ of degree at most $q-1$;
\item a primitive $q$-th root of unity $\zeta\in K$;
\item an element $\omega_K\in K^*$ of order
      $q^{v_q(|K|-1)}$.
\end{itemize}
There is a deterministic algorithm, denoted by $\mathrm{OddSplit}$, that
returns a nontrivial proper monic divisor of $F$ over $\mathbb F_p$ in a
number of bit operations bounded by a fixed polynomial in $B$.

Let $h\in\mathbf F_p[X]$ be monic and square-free of degree $d$, let
$r=\dim\mathcal B_h\ge2$, and suppose $p>r^3$.  From any ordered basis
$b_0,\ldots,b_{r-1}$ of $\mathcal B_h$, one can find an integer
$t\in\{0,\ldots,r^3\}$ such that the characteristic polynomial $F_t$ of
multiplication by
\[
 b(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}t^j b_j
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal B_h
\]
is square-free.  The polynomial $F_t$ is monic, totally split over
$\mathbf F_p$, and has degree $r$.  Every nontrivial proper monic divisor
$S$ of $F_t$ gives a nontrivial proper factor
$\gcd(h,S(b(t)))$ of $h$.
The construction has bit complexity polynomial in $d$ and $\log p$.

properties.statement_tex:
Let \(r\ge0\) and \(D\ge1\) be integers, and let \(m\) consist of the
\[
 l=\sum_{j=1}^{\min(2D,r)}\binom rj
\]
nonempty sign moments.  Let \(M(m)\) be their moment matrix, of
dimension
\[
 G=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(D,r)}\binom rj.
\]
Suppose a finite list of rational affine inequalities
\(\ell_t(m)\le b_t\) is given, each with nonconstant coefficient vector
of \(\ell^1\)-norm at most \(1\), together with a dyadic
\(0<\zeta\le1/4\).

There is a deterministic rational procedure which either returns a
vector satisfying
\[
 m\in[-1,1]^l,\qquad M(m)\succeq0,\qquad \ell_t(m)\le b_t
 \quad\text{for all }t,
\]
or reports failure.  It returns a vector whenever some
\(m^*\in[-1,1]^l\) satisfies
\[
 M(m^*)\succeq(\zeta/8)\operatorname{Id}_G,\qquad
 \ell_t(m^*)\le b_t-\zeta/2\quad\text{for all }t.
\]
Put \(\lambda=\zeta/(16G)\).  The procedure performs at most
\(\lceil10(1+l)/\lambda^2\rceil\) feasibility checks, each taking a
number of bit operations polynomial in the list dimensions, the
input bit lengths, and \(\log(1/\zeta)\).  These time bounds hold
without the slack assumption.

properties.statement_tex:
There exist absolute constants $C,c\ge1$ and one randomized multitape
Turing machine $\mathcal A$ with the following property. For every
$n\ge2$, every rational $p\in(0,1]$, and every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, given
$n,p$ in binary and access to independent ordinary deletion traces of
$x$, the machine requests at most
\[
 M_C(n,p)=\left\lceil\exp\bigl(CB(n,p)\bigr)\right\rceil
\]
traces, outputs an element of $\{0,1\}^n$, and returns $x$ with probability
at least $2/3$.

For every internal random-bit sequence and every well-formed trace
stream of strings of length at most $n$, it halts within
\[
 \bigl(n+L+M_C(n,p)\bigr)^c
\]
bit operations. This bound includes preprocessing, all parameter and
finite-precision calculations, every received trace bit and delimiter,
and the output. The only oracle operation is the external generation
of the independent deletion traces.

$H\ge1$ with the following property. For $n\ge2$ and $0<p<1$, define
\[
 D_*=4^{\lceil\log_2 Y\rceil+H}\le4^{H+1}Y^2,
\]
using \eqref{eq:aux-parameters}. For every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, every
$d\in[n]$, and every positive moment functional of order $2D$ fixing
$x_1,\ldots,x_{d-1},1-x_d$, where $D\ge D_*$, some nonempty
$I\subseteq[n]$ with $|I|\le D_*$ satisfies
\[
 |\EE[T_I]-T_I(x)|>
       \exp\bigl(-C_{\mathrm{sep}}B(n,p)\bigr).
\]

properties.statement_tex:
\begin{thm}
For integer $n\ge 2$ and $0<p\le1$, worst-case trace reconstruction of
binary strings is possible in this channel with at most
\[
\exp\!\left(O\!\left(p^{-1}(\log n)^3(1+\log\log(2n))^6\right)\right)
\]
traces, with an absolute constant. Write $q=1-p$. More finely, when $q>0$, setting
$\mathcal X=1+\log n/(1+\log(1/q))$, the logarithm of the required sample
budget is at most
\[
 O\big(p^{-1}(\log n)\mathcal X^2 (1+\log\mathcal X)^6\big)
\]
with an absolute constant. In particular for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and
$0\le q\le n^{-\varepsilon}$ the number of traces can be polynomial in $n$
(with parameters of the polynomial allowed to depend on $\varepsilon$).
The same asymptotic bounds also suffice for
strings with general symbols (assuming exact observation of retained symbols).
This concerns sample complexity, not computational efficiency.
\end{thm}

For the parameters of Section~\ref{sec:scales}, let $1\le i\le D$ and suppose a level-$(i-1)$ pair satisfies Definition~\ref{def:invariant} with constants $C,\omega,M_B$.  Set
\[
 C'=\max\{C,C_{\rm abs}/\omega\}.
\]
The input pair remains valid when $C$ is replaced by $C'$, and there exists a level-$i$ pair satisfying the definition with the same constants $C',\omega,M_B$, with
\[
 d_i=d_{i-1}+(b_i-1)/4-.05,
 \qquad E_i\le\Delta+(\ell_i/\ell_{i-1})E_{i-1}.
\]
Every preceding level constructed with $C$ also remains valid with $C'$, and this enlarged value is retained in later blocks.  The conclusion is uniform over all levels along the stated joint asymptotic regime.

Let $\sigma$ be the Prouhet--Thue--Morse sequence of order $s_*$ above.  Suppose $\pi$ is an integer translation or reflection of a fair binomial probability mass function with $g\ge c_0\omega^2m$ trials, where $c_0>0$ is absolute and $m\to\infty$ as in the construction.  Then
\begin{align}
 \|\sigma*\pi\|_\infty
 &\le \exp(O((s_*+1)^2+(s_*+1)\Lambda))\,
       m^{-(s_*+1)/2},\nonumber\\
 \|\sigma*\pi\|_2^2
 &\le \exp(O((s_*+1)^2+(s_*+1)\Lambda))\,
       m^{-s_*-1/2},\qquad
 \|\pi\|_\infty\le O(\omega^{-1}m^{-1/2}).\label{eq:sig_conv}
\end{align}
The norms use counting measure on the integers, and the implicit constants may depend on $c_0$.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $t\ge2$ be an even integer, let $h\ge0$, and let $(Z_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}$ be a finite family of independent centered real variables with $\|Z_j\|_t\le h$.  For an integer $r\ge1$, the degree-$r$ multilinear
polynomial with real coefficients $A(S)$ on $r$-subsets satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:hc}
\left\|\sum_{|S|=r} A(S)\prod_{j\in S}Z_j\right\|_t
\le (C_1 t h)^r \|A\|_{\ell^2},
\end{equation}
where $\ell^2$ uses counting measure and $C_1$ is absolute.

properties.statement_tex:
Fix a level $0\le i\le D$ and its parameters from Section~\ref{sec:scales}.  Suppose preliminary oracle laws have common
``side'' metadata with law $Q_{\rm side}$, and conditional densities
$G_x,G_y$ over a conditional reference $Q$, possibly depending on
metadata.  Require $\int G_x\,dQ=\int G_y\,dQ=1$ for $Q_{\rm side}$-almost every metadata value.  Use $Q_{\rm side}Q$ as the joint reference. Suppose
on a typical metadata event of probability $\ge1-o(\Delta)$ we have
uniform estimates
\begin{equation}\label{eq:clipcond}
\|G_x-1\|_{r_i},\|G_y-1\|_{r_i}\le N_i^{-\rho},
\qquad \|G_y-G_x\|_{r_i}^2\le N_i^{-d_i-.01}
\end{equation}
in $L^{r_i}(Q)$, where $\rho\ge 2^{-4B-10}$.
Then conditioning each law on the event consisting of typical metadata and $G_x\ge1/2$ changes it in total variation by $o(\Delta)$.  The conditioned laws $\mu,\nu$ satisfy $\nu\ll\mu$ and
\[
 \|d\nu/d\mu-1\|_{L^{r_i}(\mu)}^2\le N_i^{-d_i}.
\]
All these conclusions hold uniformly over $0\le i\le D$.

such that
\[

\]

properties.statement_tex:

\cref{word:affine}.  Every column of $W$ is nonconstant if and only if
$B\ne0$.  In that case every positive vertical period of $W$ is
divisible by $p$.

properties.statement_tex:

properties.statement: Last nonzero p-adic digit f(m),f(0)=1,negative integers allowed; W(n,m)=f(m) satisfies all integer-slope line rules and all columns nonconstant. Not a finite patch simulation/proof of practical tile size.
properties.statement_tex:
For $t\in\Z\setminus\{0\}$, let $\operatorname{ord}_p(t)$ be the
largest nonnegative integer $r$ for which $p^r\mid t$, and define
\[
    f(t)=\frac{t}{p^{\operatorname{ord}_p(t)}}\pmod p,
    \qquad f(0)=1.
\]
Then $f\colon\Z\to\Sigma$, and the array $W(n,m)=f(m)$ satisfies the
line rule and has every column nonconstant.
properties.title: A model for the line rule

conditions: Assuming graph equation A+H0 exact,one finite dependence tile enforces c_i(b-sigma)=c_i(b) for chosen base shift,leaving other outputs/high/z unrestricted. Two pieces partition H0 and shifted zero-output slice.

properties.statement_tex:
Fix a channel $i$ and a shift $\sigma\in\Z^2\times K$.
There is a finite nonempty tile $F_{i,\sigma}\subset G$ such that,
for every graph satisfying \eqref{enc:graph},
\[
 A\oplus F_{i,\sigma}=G
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 c_i(b-\sigma)=c_i(b)\text{ for every }b\in\Z^2\times K.
\]
This equation imposes no restriction on the graph's other outputs.

properties.statement_tex:
Fix $i,j$, a target horizontal coordinate $x_1\in\Z$, and a target
low coordinate $k_i\in K_i$.  For each $(l,\delta)\in K_i\times\Delta_i$,
choose an integer $h_1(l,\delta)$ satisfying
\[
 h_1(l,\delta)\equiv l\pmod{r_i},\qquad
 h_1(l,\delta)\equiv\rho^a(\delta)\pmod{a_i},\qquad
 h_1(l,\delta)\equiv\rho^b(\delta)\pmod{b_i}.
\]
Then the map
\begin{equation}\label{model:block-map}
 (l,\delta)\longmapsto
 \left(
 C_{i,j}(k_i-l)+e_\delta,
 T_{i,j}\bigl(x_1-h_1(l,\delta)\bigr)(k_i-l)
 \right)
\end{equation}
is a bijection from $K_i\times\Delta_i$ to $P_i\times K_i$.

conditions: For abelian H,finite nonempty F_nu and full-difference partition,stack Fst=union F_nu x E_nu tiles H x Z/q iff ONE A solves every equation in H. Periodic tiling gives periodic common complement and conversely. Injective projection and fibre cardinalities essential.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $H$ be an abelian group, let $F_1,\ldots,F_s\subset H$ be finite
nonempty sets, and let $E_1,\ldots,E_s$ be a partition as in
\cref{stack:partition}.  Define
\[
 F^{\mathrm{st}}=\bigcup_{\nu=1}^s(F_\nu\times E_\nu)
 \subset H\times\Zmod{q}.
\]
There is a common solution to $A\oplus F_\nu=H$ for all $\nu$ if and
only if $F^{\mathrm{st}}$ tiles $H\times\Zmod{q}$.  Moreover, a
fully periodic tiling by $F^{\mathrm{st}}$ gives a fully periodic
common solution, and a fully periodic common solution gives a fully
periodic tiling by $F^{\mathrm{st}}$.
properties.title: Stacking and periodicity

properties.statement_tex:
\begin{maintheorem}
There is a \(C^\infty\) positive definite Riemannian metric \(g\) on
\((-1,1)^2\) such that no open neighborhood \(U\) of the origin admits a
\(C^\infty\) isometric immersion
\[
F:(U,g)\longrightarrow\R^3.
\]
In particular, no such neighborhood admits a smooth isometric embedding.
\end{maintheorem}

Let \(K_0\in C^\infty((-1,1)^2)\) with
\(\norm{K_0}_\infty\le10^{-3}\).

\]
whose curvature is \(K_0\). Its eigenvalues have positive uniform
lower and upper bounds.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $E,F$ be smooth Hermitian complex vector bundles of ranks $d,r$ over
a compact smooth manifold $Y$ of real dimension $2h$, and let $q\geq1$.
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite set of integer pairs $(s,t)$ with
$1\leq s\leq d$ and $0\leq t\leq r$ such that
\begin{equation}
  (qs-t)(r-t)-s(d-s)>h
  \qquad ((s,t)\in\mathcal A).
  \label{eq:incidence-dimension}
\end{equation}
There are smooth bundle maps $T_1,\ldots,T_q:E\to F$ such that, for every
$y\in Y$, every $(s,t)\in\mathcal A$, and every complex $s$-plane
$S\subset E_y$,
\[
  \dim_{\mathbb C}\sum_{i=1}^q T_i(y)S>t.
\]
Here and below the sum denotes linear span.  The same statement holds
over a point, with $h=0$.

Let $B$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra, let $N\ge1$, and suppose
$x_1,\ldots,x_N\in B$ satisfy
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^N x_i^*x_i=1,
  \qquad
  \sum_{i=1}^N x_ix_i^*\le c1
  \quad\text{for some }0\le c<1.
\]
There are positive contractions $a,b\in M_{2N}(B)$, determined by this
tuple, such that every normalized $1$-quasitrace $\tau$ on $M_{2N}(B)$
satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \tau(a+b)-\tau(a)-\tau(b)\ge\frac{1-c}{2N}.
  \label{eq:uniform-defect}
\end{equation}

result: Sage实际接受给定的完整环映射并计算逆：inverse先检验单射，再为每个陪域生成元求原像，缺原像报不满射；is_invertible分别检查两者。其现有文档明确举例同一多项式映射在原环不可逆、商环可逆，没有把商同构冒充环境自同构。已知完整映射与“寻找其余分量使一个f成为坐标”是不同问题，给定映射求逆失败不证明f非坐标。
Sage的图理想包含两边关系，商环时必要时回到覆盖环消元；默认通过Gröbner正规形求原像，并缓存相关对象。支持范围包含整数和部分商环，源码有零环、非约化商及QQbar例，不能一概说只支持域。实际要求交换、同基环、平凡基映射、全局项序及已实现的reduce；任意CommRing或参数域并无统一运行保证。完整单射后端和Singular依赖未读，未执行这些文档例。

Singular实际alg_kernel／is_injective／is_surjective／is_bijective用关系与标准基、正规形，区分基环和源环；目标qring保留定义理想，源为商环时核再模I检查。它明确提示源商映射还需良定义、局部／混合项序下返回1须谨慎解释，不能把未验证的源关系当同构证书。完整algDependent、create_ring、NF和标准基后端未读，未据此声称所有设置已证明正确或发现软件错误。
旧方法对照更强：已有图理想消元、逐生成元原像和双向复合可核验给定商同构／完整环境映射。F049显式Bézout和无除法公式可形成另一条证书路径，但寻找证书、关系核验、表达式膨胀、正规形和所有反向复合的成本必须统一计；仅在已知公式上重算恒等式不是新应用增益。原文任意交换环引理不自动赋予CAS对所有交换环的实现。
Edo–Vénéreau2001原始Theorem7另作选读：该文A×表示非零因子而非单位；p非零因子、a模p为单位、G各系数模p幂零且F已经是变量时，aF+G+px为变量。旧transfer有这些条件，不是任意坐标判定器或删除稳定变量规则。它匹配十月源文H=L-u+pQ0的旧结构步骤，不将旧定理或本包源码审核计为新数值验证。
结论：两个问题及消费者／强旧成本闸门仍未建立，降低直接数值优先级，保留可重访条件。没有观察到这两CAS把纤维或稳定证书误判为环境坐标，也没有新候选、初检或实验。下一份资源应回到未覆盖代数／拓扑或实复分析；本包之后立即进行全局复盘025。

conditions: Old Matolcsi-Ruzsa-type lower bound for finite D with C elements and affine real dimension h: |kD|>=binom(k+h,h)+(C-1-h)binom(k+h-1,h). Triangulation includes every point, and half-open assignments avoid double counts. This lemma is not a new F210 application improvement.
properties.statement: Old Matolcsi-Ruzsa-type lower bound for finite D with C elements and affine real dimension h: |kD|>=binom(k+h,h)+(C-1-h)binom(k+h-1,h). Triangulation includes every point, and half-open assignments avoid double counts. This lemma is not a new F210 application improvement.
properties.statement_tex:
Let \(D\) be a nonempty finite set of \(C\) points in a real vector space,
of affine dimension \(h\). Write
\(kD=\{v_1+\cdots+v_k:v_1,\ldots,v_k\in D\}\).
For this \(k\)-fold sumset, \(k\ge1\), one has
\[
 |kD|\ \ge\
 f(C,h,k):=\binom{k+h}{h}+(C-1-h)\binom{k+h-1}{h}.
\]
properties.title: Sumsets

conditions: From Q(x)>=C>0 with positive degree d0=w(x)/6, choose z=min(18,min{h:binom(d0+h,h)>=C}); Q(kx)>=f(C,z,k). Row-reduced distinct leading monomials give C exponent vectors on degree d0 hyperplane and affine dimension>=z; distinct SUMS certify independent products. Does not assert C^k independent products. Cap18 weakens a lower bound.
properties.statement: From Q(x)>=C>0 with positive degree d0=w(x)/6, choose z=min(18,min{h:binom(d0+h,h)>=C}); Q(kx)>=f(C,z,k). Row-reduced distinct leading monomials give C exponent vectors on degree d0 hyperplane and affine dimension>=z; distinct SUMS certify independent products. Does not assert C^k independent products. Cap18 weakens a lower bound.
properties.statement_tex:
Suppose \(Q(x)\ge C>0\), where \(C\) is an integer and
\(w(x)=6d_0\) with \(d_0>0\). Put
\[
 z=\min\left(18,\ \min\left\{h\ge0:
                              \binom{d_0+h}{h}\ge C\right\}\right).
\]
Then for all \(k\ge1\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:power}
                Q(kx)\ge f(C,z,k).
\end{equation}
properties.title: Power certificate

conditions: For |gamma|-|mu|=i b, coefficient [s_gamma] h_b(X^i)s_mu belongs to{0,+1,-1}. Nonzero requires gamma_j>=mu_j>=gamma_(j+i) and residue matching; determinant sorting determines sign. Do not drop signs or transfer to arbitrary plethysm coefficients.
properties.statement: For |gamma|-|mu|=i b, coefficient [s_gamma] h_b(X^i)s_mu belongs to{0,+1,-1}. Nonzero requires gamma_j>=mu_j>=gamma_(j+i) and residue matching; determinant sorting determines sign. Do not drop signs or transfer to arbitrary plethysm coefficients.
properties.statement_tex:
Let \(\gamma,\mu\) be partitions of length at most \(n\), and suppose
\(|\gamma|-|\mu|=ib\), where \(i,b\ge1\). Then
\[
                  [s_\gamma]\,h_b(X^i)s_\mu(X)\in\{0,1,-1\}.
\]
For a nonzero coefficient one necessarily has
\[
        \gamma_j\ge\mu_j,\qquad \mu_j\ge\gamma_{j+i}
                         \quad\text{whenever the subscripts are in range}.
\]
Here \(X^i=(x_1^i,\ldots,x_n^i)\).

properties.statement_tex:
For every integer \(b\ge6\) and every finite-dimensional complex vector
space \(V\), there is a \(\GL(V)\)-equivariant injection
\[
                 \Sym^6(\Sym^b V)\ \hookrightarrow\ \Sym^b(\Sym^6 V).
\]
Equivalently, \(h_b[h_6]-h_6[h_b]\) is Schur-positive for every \(b\ge6\).

properties.statement_tex:
Let \(c,d\in\NN^6\) satisfy \(6\mid w(c)\) and \(6\mid w(d)\).
If \(Q(c)>0\), then \(Q(d+c)\ge Q(d)\). In particular
\[
          Q(d+6e_i)\ge Q(d)\quad(1\le i\le6),
          \qquad F(d+6e_6)=F(d).
\]

properties.statement: For a>=2, finite V and f in equal-row degree k invariant R_k, z(v)^L f lies in A_(k+L) if k+L>=a k, where A is generated by R_1 and z(v)=v tensor a. Local chart requires nonzero v, and ratio invariant of total degree t uses <=t polarized elementary factors. Cancellation in a polynomial domain; no numeric condition estimate.
properties.statement_tex:
For every integer \(t\ge0\), every row-permutation-invariant polynomial
in the lists \(Y_i\) of total degree at most \(t\) is a linear combination of products of at
most \(t\) elements of \(z^{-1}R_1\).
Consequently, for integers \(k,L\ge0\) and \(f\in R_k\),
\[
             z^Lf\in A_{k+L}\qquad\text{if }k+L\ge ak.
\]

properties.statement: For L>=1 and j>=a L, W_j is spanned by z(v)^L W_(j-L) over all v; averaging yields the R analogue. Iterated directional derivatives use strictly positive source-minus-destination degree at every shift. Field C and polarization factorials matter.
properties.statement_tex:

\[
       W_j=\sum_{v\in V}z(v)^L W_{j-L},
       \qquad
       R_j=\sum_{v\in V}z(v)^L R_{j-L}.
\]
The sums mean linear spans.

in $U$ and degree $q$ in $Y$, the operator $\D{Y}{U}$ is injective if
$p>q$. The polynomials may depend on any finite collection of additional
variables independent of $U$ and $Y$.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space, and let $a\ge1$ and
$b\ge1$ be integers satisfying $b\ge a(a-1)$.
If a symmetric $a$-linear form $T$ on $\Sym^b V$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diagonal}
 T(P,\ldots,P)=0
 \qquad\text{for every product $P$ of $b$ vectors},
\end{equation}
then $T=0$.

properties.statement_tex:
For every $n\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$, the classes
$(C_n,W_n,F_n)$ in \eqref{eq:prescribed-classes} form a proper
combinatorial model structure on $\nCat$. It is cofibrantly generated by
$(L_nI,L_nJ)$, where
\[
 I=\{\partial\Delta[m]\hookrightarrow\Delta[m]:m\ge0\},\qquad
 J=\{\Lambda^k[m]\hookrightarrow\Delta[m]:m\ge1,\ 0\le k\le m\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 L_n:\sSet_{\KQ}\rightleftarrows(\nCat,C_n,W_n,F_n):R_n
\]
is a Quillen equivalence.

properties.statement: Right Gray internal hom H(Y)=Hom_oplax(D1,Y) is an n-category for finite n targetY; reflection X->tau_nX gives natural bijection of cylinders intoY preserving endpoints/restrictions. Tensor stays in omega-category and may contain dimension n+1 cells. Reflection identifies n-cell boundaries of(n+1)cells; not the q-cell-preserving unique-filler cutoff.
properties.statement_tex:
Let $n<\infty$ and let $Y$ be a strict $n$-category.  Then $H(Y)$ is a
strict $n$-category.  Consequently the reflection unit $X\to\trunc X$
induces a natural bijection
\begin{equation}\label{eq:truncated-cylinder-bijection}
 \Hom_{\omCat}((\trunc X)\otimes\Disk{1},Y)
 \ \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\
 \Hom_{\omCat}(X\otimes\Disk{1},Y).
\end{equation}
This bijection respects endpoints and restriction along functors in
the first variable.  For $n=\infty$ the same assertion holds with
$\trunc=\id$.
properties.title: Internal hom and reflection

conditions: Natural map N_inftyX x Delta1 -> N_infty(X tensor D1), endpoint/counit formulas, yields nerve homotopy; stationary strict functor restricts to constant old-nerve homotopy. Positive Alexander-Whitney diagonal is natural for monotone ordinal maps including degeneracies, not arbitrary chain maps. Right interval convention fixed.
properties.statement: Natural map N_inftyX x Delta1 -> N_infty(X tensor D1), endpoint/counit formulas, yields nerve homotopy; stationary strict functor restricts to constant old-nerve homotopy. Positive Alexander-Whitney diagonal is natural for monotone ordinal maps including degeneracies, not arbitrary chain maps. Right interval convention fixed.
properties.statement_tex:
There is a natural simplicial map
\[
 J_X:N_\infty X\times\Delta[1]\longrightarrow
           N_\infty(X\otimes\Disk{1})
\]
whose restriction at the endpoint $a$ is
$N_\infty(\id_X\otimes e_a)$, and for which
$N_\infty(\pi_X)J_X$ is the projection to $N_\infty X$.
Consequently a strict functor $P:X\otimes\Disk{1}\to Y$ induces a
simplicial homotopy between the nerves of its endpoint functors.
If a functor $a:A\to X$ satisfies
$P(a\otimes\id)=h\pi_A$ for some $h:A\to Y$, the homotopy restricts
along $N_\infty a$ to the constant homotopy of $N_\infty h$.
The same assertions apply to $\Street$ when $X,Y$ are $n$-categories.
properties.title: A right Gray cylinder gives a nerve homotopy

conditions: Strict n-categories locally finitely presentable; filtered colimits computed on cells, each reflected finite oriental finitely presentable, Street nerve and finite Ex iterates preserve filtered colimits. Simplicial weak equivalences closed under filtered colimits of arrows without injective transition maps. Finite support/equality witnesses, not finite object cardinality.

properties.statement_tex:
For every $1\le n\le\infty$, the category $\nCat$ is locally finitely
presentable, and filtered colimits are computed on cells.
Each $\trunc\Orient{m}$ is finitely presentable in $\nCat$.
Consequently $\Street$, and also $\Ex^r\Street$ for every finite
$r\ge0$, preserve filtered colimits.  Simplicial weak equivalences
are closed under filtered colimits of arrows, as are the maps
$f$ of $\nCat$ for which $\Street f$ is a weak equivalence.
No monomorphism hypothesis on transition maps is required.
properties.title: Presentability and filtered colimits

conditions: Map of spans of simplicial sets with three objectwise weak equivalences and ONE SPECIFIED MONOMORPHIC leg in each row gives pushout weak equivalence; ordinary pushouts compute homotopy pushouts. Other attaching leg may be nonmonic. Uses old simplicial left properness/cofibrant undercategories, not unconditional weak-equivalence preservation for arbitrary pushouts.
properties.statement: Map of spans of simplicial sets with three objectwise weak equivalences and ONE SPECIFIED MONOMORPHIC leg in each row gives pushout weak equivalence; ordinary pushouts compute homotopy pushouts. Other attaching leg may be nonmonic. Uses old simplicial left properness/cofibrant undercategories, not unconditional weak-equivalence preservation for arbitrary pushouts.
properties.statement_tex:
Consider a commutative map of spans of simplicial sets
\[
 \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large]
 A \arrow[d,"a"'] &
 C \arrow[l] \arrow[r,hook,"i"] \arrow[d,"c"'] &
 B \arrow[d,"b"]\\
 A' &
 C' \arrow[l] \arrow[r,hook,"i'"'] &
 B'.
 \end{tikzcd}
\]
where $i$ and $i'$ are monomorphisms.
If $a,b,c$ are weak equivalences, then the canonical map
\[
 A\amalg_C B\longrightarrow A'\amalg_{C'}B'
\]
is a weak equivalence.  There is no condition on the maps $C\to A$
and $C'\to A'$.  Each of the displayed ordinary pushouts computes a
homotopy pushout.  In particular, cobase change of a weak equivalence
along a simplicial monomorphism is a weak equivalence.
properties.title: Gluing with one monomorphic leg

conditions: A sieve A in posetE, monotone f<=g, f|A=g|A, g constant on E minusA: positive normalized chain formula [w] tensor u ->[f(w0),...,f(wp),g(wp)] defines strict RIGHT Gray cylinder, stationary relative to common endpoint map on all U(A). Agreement on all chain degrees/degeneracies essential. A zero top chain can be identity on a NONidentity lower cell; top-chain zero alone does not prove full stationarity.
properties.statement: A sieve A in posetE, monotone f<=g, f|A=g|A, g constant on E minusA: positive normalized chain formula [w] tensor u ->[f(w0),...,f(wp),g(wp)] defines strict RIGHT Gray cylinder, stationary relative to common endpoint map on all U(A). Agreement on all chain degrees/degeneracies essential. A zero top chain can be identity on a NONidentity lower cell; top-chain zero alone does not prove full stationarity.
properties.statement_tex:
Let $A\subset E$ be a downward-closed subposet, and let $f,g:E\to E$
be monotone maps such that
\[
 f(e)\le g(e)\quad(e\in E),\qquad f|_A=g|_A,
 \qquad g|_{E\setminus A}\text{ is constant}.
\]
The constancy condition is vacuous when $E\setminus A$ is empty.
For each $1\le n\le\infty$ there is a strict functor of
$\omega$-categories
\[
 P_{f,g}:\U{E}\otimes\Disk{1}\longrightarrow\U{E}
\]
whose restrictions to the two interval endpoints are $U(f)$ and
$U(g)$.  If $i:A\hookrightarrow E$ and $v=f i=g i:A\to E$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prism-stationarity}
 P_{f,g}(U(i)\otimes\id_{\Disk{1}})=U(v)\pi_{\U{A}}.
\end{equation}
Consequently its endpoints induce simplicially homotopic maps on
Street nerves, with the homotopy stationary relative to $\Street U(v)$.
properties.title: Relative prism

conditions: For arbitrary strict i:B0->B and attachment a:B0->X, endpointF0i=F1i=i plus strict stationarity P(i tensor1)=i pi glues cylinder to constant one onX across actual nCat pushout. Transpose into H(Y), an n-category. No injectivity/freeness/cofibrancy needed. A mere homotopy of endpoint nerves without strict old-side equality is insufficient.
properties.statement: For arbitrary strict i:B0->B and attachment a:B0->X, endpointF0i=F1i=i plus strict stationarity P(i tensor1)=i pi glues cylinder to constant one onX across actual nCat pushout. Transpose into H(Y), an n-category. No injectivity/freeness/cofibrancy needed. A mere homotopy of endpoint nerves without strict old-side equality is insufficient.
properties.statement_tex:
Let $i:B_0\to B$ and $a:B_0\to X$ be arbitrary strict functors of
$n$-categories, and form the pushout
\[
 \begin{tikzcd}
 B_0\ar[r,"i"]\ar[d,"a"']&B\ar[d,"b"]\\
 X\ar[r,"j"']&Y.
 \end{tikzcd}
\]
Suppose $F_0,F_1:B\to B$ satisfy $F_0i=F_1i=i$, and suppose
$P:B\otimes\Disk{1}\to B$ has endpoints $F_0,F_1$ and satisfies
$P(i\otimes\id)=i\pi_{B_0}$.
Then there is a cylinder $Q:Y\otimes\Disk{1}\to Y$ stationary on $X$,
whose endpoints $\overline F_0,\overline F_1:Y\to Y$ are specified by
\[
 \overline F_\delta j=j,\qquad
 \overline F_\delta b=bF_\delta\qquad(\delta=0,1).
\]
Its restriction along $b\otimes\id$ is $bP$.
This construction is natural in $a:B_0\to X$, and its nerve gives a
simplicial homotopy between $\Street\overline F_0$ and
$\Street\overline F_1$ stationary along $\Street j$.
In particular it applies to Lemma~\ref{lem:relative-prism} whenever
$f|_A=g|_A=\id_A$, for every attaching functor $\U{A}\to X$.
properties.title: Gluing a stationary cylinder

properties.statement_tex:
For $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$, the functor
\[
 F_\epsilon:\nCat/\Disk{1}\longrightarrow\nCat,
 \qquad (C\xrightarrow{p}\Disk{1})\longmapsto C_\epsilon=p^{-1}(\epsilon),
\]
preserves all small colimits.  The object functor
$\operatorname{Ob}:\nCat\to\mathrm{Set}$ also preserves all small colimits.
Both assertions hold directly for $n=\infty$.
properties.title: Fibers and objects preserve colimits

properties.statement_tex:
Let $I$ be an initial or a final segment of $[m]=\{0,\ldots,m\}$.
If $I$ is nonempty and has $q+1$ vertices, the face inclusion identifies
$\trunc\Orient{q}$ with the full sub-$n$-category of
$\trunc\Orient{m}$ on $I$.  If $I$ is empty, that full subcategory is
empty.  Here and below $\trunc=\id$ when $n=\infty$.
properties.title: Full oriental segments

properties.statement_tex:
There is a canonical identification $\operatorname{Ob}\U{P}=P$ for
every poset $P$.  If $S\subset P$ is a sieve, the map
$\U{S}\to\U{P}$ is the inclusion of the full $0$-fiber of the membership
label $\U{P}\to\Disk{1}$.  If $S$ is a cosieve, it is the inclusion
of the full $1$-fiber.  These identifications are natural for maps of
labelled posets and include empty posets and empty fibers.
properties.title: Poset pieces

properties.statement_tex:
Let $A\subset P$ be a full subposet, let $a:\U{A}\to X$ be any strict
functor, and form
\[
 Y=X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{P}.
\]
Suppose a monotone map $\lambda:P\to[1]$ and a strict functor
$\xi:X\to\Disk{1}$ satisfy
\[
 \xi a=U(\lambda|_A):\U{A}\longrightarrow\Disk{1},
 \qquad \U{[1]}=\Disk{1}.
\]
Write
$P_\epsilon=\lambda^{-1}(\epsilon)$,
$A_\epsilon=A\cap P_\epsilon$, and
$X_\epsilon=\xi^{-1}(\epsilon)$.  Then the induced label
$Y\to\Disk{1}$ has actual full fibers
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pushout-fiber}
 Y_\epsilon\cong
 X_\epsilon\amalg_{\U{A_\epsilon}}\U{P_\epsilon}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, independently of these labels,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pushout-objects}
 \operatorname{Ob}Y\cong
 \operatorname{Ob}X\amalg_A P
 \cong\operatorname{Ob}X\amalg(P\setminus A).
\end{equation}
For two such pairs of compatible labels, write
$\bar\lambda_1,\bar\lambda_2:Y\to\Disk{1}$ for the induced labels.
Their $0$-fibers intersect in the $0$-fiber of
$\max\circ(\bar\lambda_1,\bar\lambda_2)$; their $1$-fibers intersect
in the $1$-fiber of $\min\circ(\bar\lambda_1,\bar\lambda_2)$.
Formula~\eqref{eq:pushout-fiber}, using the corresponding maximum or
minimum on both original legs, computes these intersections as well.

properties.statement_tex:
With the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:labelled-pushout}, the
following are canonical identifications of subcategories of $Y$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Suppose $P_1,P_2$ are sieves of $P$, contain $A$, and cover $P$.
Then the subcategories
\[
 Y_i=X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{P_i}\quad(i=1,2)
\]
are sieves covering $Y$ on objects, and
\[
 Y_1\cap Y_2
 =X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{P_1\cap P_2}.
\]
\item Suppose $T_1,T_2$ are cosieves of $P$, cover $P$, satisfy
$A\subset T_1$, and satisfy $A\cap T_2=\varnothing$.  Then
\[
 Y_1=X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{T_1},\qquad Y_2=\U{T_2}
\]
are cosieves covering $Y$ on objects, and
$Y_1\cap Y_2=\U{T_1\cap T_2}$.
\end{enumerate}
If $A$ itself is a sieve of $P$, the canonical map $X\to Y$ is the
inclusion of a full sieve.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $C_1,C_2\subset C$ be two full sieves which cover the objects of
$C$, or two full cosieves which cover its objects.  Put
$C_{12}=C_1\cap C_2$.  The square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
 \Street C_{12} \ar[r,hook] \ar[d,hook] & \Street C_2 \ar[d,hook] \\
 \Street C_1 \ar[r,hook] & \Street C
\end{tikzcd}
\]
is an ordinary pushout of simplicial sets.  All four maps are
monomorphisms, so it is also a homotopy pushout in the Kan--Quillen
model structure.

retraction $p:Y\to X$ such that $\Street(jp)$ and $\id_{\Street Y}$ are
joined by a zigzag of simplicial homotopies.  Consequently $j$ is a
Thomason equivalence.  Neither $A$ nor $E$ needs to be finite.

Let $A\subset B$ be a sieve of small posets.  Let $Z$ be its upward
closure, and suppose that $A\hookrightarrow Z$ admits a right adjoint
retraction.  For every functor $a:\U{A}\to X$ in $\nCat$, put
\[
 V_B(X)=X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{B},\qquad
 P_B(X)=\Street X\amalg_{\Street\U{A}}\Street\U{B}.
\]
The canonical map
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_{B,X}:P_B(X)\longrightarrow\Street V_B(X)
 \label{eq:attachment-comparison}
\end{equation}
is a simplicial weak equivalence.  The map
$\Street\U{A}\to\Street\U{B}$ is a monomorphism.
The comparison is natural in every functor $f:X\to X'$ under
$\U{A}$.

or a horn inclusion $\Lambda^k[m]\hookrightarrow\Delta[m]$, with
$m\geq1$ and $0\leq k\leq m$.  There are finite posets $A\subset B$
and a canonical identification
\[
 \Sd^2 d=\bigl(\OrdN A\hookrightarrow\OrdN B\bigr).
\]
Here $A$ is a sieve.  Its upward closure $Z$ in $B$ is a cosieve, and
$A\hookrightarrow Z$ has a right adjoint retraction.

properties.statement_tex:
For real $u\in W^{1,1}(\R^2)$ there are real
$u_j\in C_c^\infty(\R^2)$ converging to $u$ in $W^{1,1}$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-translation}
 \|u(\cdot+z)-u\|_1\le |z|\,\|\nabla u\|_1
 \qquad(z\in\R^2).
\end{equation}
Moreover $|u|\in W^{1,1}(\R^2)$ with
$|\nabla|u||\le|\nabla u|$ almost everywhere. If $\chi$ is
smooth and compactly supported, then $\chi u\in W^{1,1}$ and
$\nabla(\chi u)=\chi\nabla u+u\nabla\chi$.
For locally Lipschitz real functions $v,w$, their maximum is
locally Lipschitz and satisfies, almost everywhere,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-maximum}
 \nabla\max(v,w)=
 \begin{cases}
  \nabla v,&v>w,\\
  \nabla w,&w>v,\\
  \nabla v=\nabla w,&v=w.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Products of locally Lipschitz functions satisfy the weak product
rule. Their weak derivatives agree almost everywhere with their
classical derivatives.

For a square $Q$ of side length $t>0$ and
$u\in W^{1,1}(\R^2)$, write $u_Q=|Q|^{-1}\int_Qu$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-poincare}
 \int_Q|u-u_Q|\le Ct\int_Q|\nabla u|.
\end{equation}
For every grid square $Q$ of side $t$, there is a smooth cutoff
$\chi_Q$ equal to one on the closed concentric dilation $3Q$,
supported in the interior of $5Q$, with $0\le\chi_Q\le1$ and
$|\nabla\chi_Q|\le C/t$. With $c_Q=u_{5Q}$, it satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-localization}
 \|\nabla[\chi_Q(u-c_Q)]\|_1
       \le C\int_{5Q}|\nabla u|.
\end{equation}
Every disk of radius at most $t$ centered in $Q$ lies in $3Q$.
The dilations $5Q$ of grid squares have bounded overlap. If the
squares under consideration meet
$O\subset\{x:\dist(x,K)<t\}$, all their dilations $5Q$ lie in
$\{x:\dist(x,K)<6t\}$. Constants are independent of
$Q,t,u,O,K$.

properties.statement_tex:
Suppose $u_j\in W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^2)$ converge locally
in $L^1$ to $u$, and
$\sup_j\int_{\R^2}|\nabla u_j|\le M<\infty$.
Then the distributional gradient of $u$ is a finite vector Radon
measure $H$, with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-local-lsc}
 |H|(\R^2)\le M,\qquad
 |H|(O)=\mathcal V(u;O)
       \le\liminf_j\int_O|\nabla u_j|
 \quad\text{for every open }O.
\end{equation}
If $|H|(K)=0$ for every compact Lebesgue-null set $K$, then
$H=G\,\dd x$ for some $G\in L^1(\R^2;\R^2)$ and
$\|G\|_1=|H|(\R^2)$. In that case
$u\in W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, with weak gradient $G$.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $BV(\R^2)$ denote the globally integrable functions whose
distributional derivatives have finite total variation. For every
real $f\in BV(\R^2)$,
\[
 Mf\in L^2(\R^2)\cap BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^2),
 \qquad |D(Mf)|(\R^2)\le C|Df|(\R^2),
\]
with the constant from Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
Writing $P(F)=|D\1_F|(\R^2)$ for perimeter, every measurable
set $E$ with $|E|<\infty$ and $P(E)<\infty$ satisfies
\[
 \int_0^1 P(\{M\1_E>t\})\,\dd t\le CP(E).
\]
These superlevel sets have finite measure for every $t>0$ and
finite perimeter for almost every $t>0$.

 \label{eq:labels-spatial-comparison}

properties.statement_tex:
Let $Q$ be a square of side length one and let
$\Omega=\{y:\dist(y,Q)<10\}$. Suppose that, on $\Omega$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-decomposition}
h=\sum_i v_i\sigma_i+\beta,
\qquad \beta=\sum_d\beta_d.
\end{equation}
The sums are finite. The measures in the sums are finite, defined on
$\R^2$, and absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.
Each $\sigma_i$ is nonnegative and each $v_i$ is a constant unit vector.
For each $d$, write $m_d=|\beta_d|(\R^2)$ and assign a number
$s_d\in(0,1]$. If $s_d<1$, assume that
$\beta_d(\R^2)=0$ and that $\beta_d$ is supported in a ball of radius
at most $C_s s_d$, where $C_s$ is fixed. Set
\[
S=\sum_i\sigma_i,
\qquad A=\sum_d s_d^\alpha m_d.
\]
For $x\in Q$, define
\begin{align*}
\mathcal I(x)
&=\{r\in[1,2]:u_r(x)\ge u_t(x)
                 \text{ for every }t>0\text{ with }|t-r|\le1/4\},\\
\mathcal J(x)
&=\{r\in[1,2]:u_r(x)=\max_{1\le t\le2}u_t(x)\}\cup\{1,2\}.
\end{align*}
Then the following estimates hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Unfavorable directional gradients.} If $e$ is a unit vector and $e\cdot v_i\ge\kappa>0$ for all $i$,
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-direction}
\int_Q\sup_{r\in\mathcal I(x)}
                  (-e\cdot\nabla u_r(x))_+\,dx\le C A.
\end{equation}
\item \emph{Band maxima and forced endpoints.} Without a condition on the directions $v_i$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-size}
\int_Q\sup_{r\in\mathcal J(x)}|\nabla u_r(x)|\,dx
    \le C\bigl(A+S(\R^2)\bigr).
\end{equation}
\item \emph{Differences of nearby averages.} We also have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-value}
\int_Q\sup_{0<t,t'\le4}|u_t(x)-u_{t'}(x)|\,dx
    \le C\bigl(A+S(\R^2)\bigr).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Here $C$ depends only on $C_s$, and in the first estimate also on
$\kappa$. A supremum of nonnegative quantities over an empty set is zero.

properties.statement_tex:
Suppose that $r\in[1,2]$ and $0<\delta\le1/4$, and that
\[
u_r(x)\ge u_{r-\delta}(x),\qquad u_r(x)\ge u_{r+\delta}(x).
\]
There is a probability
density $k$ supported on $[r-\delta,r+\delta]$, bounded by $C/\delta$,
such that
\[
K(y)=\int k(t)\mathbf1_{B(x,t)}(y)\,dt
\]
satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-zero-moment}
\int K(y)\overline{y-x}\,dh(y)=0.
\end{equation}
Moreover, $0\le K\le1$, $\Lip(K)\le C/\delta$,
$K=1$ on $B(x,r-\delta)$, and $K=0$ outside $B(x,r+\delta)$.
The density may be chosen measurably in $(x,r)$.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $x\in\R^2$, $r\in[1,2]$, $0<\delta\le1/4$, and
\[
 D=\{y:\bigl||y-x|-r\bigr|\le\delta\}.
\]
Let $h$ be a complex measure whose variation is finite on $B(x,3)$.
Suppose that $K_0,K_1:\R^2\to[0,1]$ are Borel functions supported in
$B(x,3)$, that $K_1-K_0$ is supported in $D$, and that
\[
 \int K_i(y)\overline{y-x}\,dh(y)=0\qquad(i=0,1).
\]
Set $P_i=\int K_i\,dh$. For every $z\in D$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-affine-identity}
 P_1-P_0=\int
 \left(1-\frac{\overline{y-x}}{\overline{z-x}}\right)
 (K_1-K_0)(y)\,dh(y).
\end{equation}
For every $0<\rho\le1$, this implies
\begin{align}\label{eq:local-affine-bound}
 |P_1-P_0|\le{}&2\rho\int_{D\cap B(z,\rho)}
                    |K_1-K_0|\,d|h|\notag\\
 &+10\int_{D\setminus B(z,\rho)}|K_1-K_0|\,d|h|.
\end{align}

properties.statement_tex:
Let $S$ and $\nu$ be finite positive Borel measures on $\R^2$, let
$U>0$ and $T\ge0$, and suppose that
\[
0<\rho\le1,
\qquad 0<\delta\le\frac{\rho^2}{1600}.
\]
Write
\[
D(x,r,\delta)=\{y:\bigl||y-x|-r\bigr|\le\delta\}.
\]
There is a Borel set $E\subset\R^2$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:shell-exception}
|E|\le C\left[
  \left(\frac{\nu(\R^2)}{U}\right)^2\frac{\delta}{\rho}
  +\frac{\nu(\R^2)}{U}\frac{\delta}{\rho^2}
           \left(1+\frac{T}{U}\right)\right],
\end{equation}
and the following implication holds for every $x\notin E$ and every
$r\in[1,2]$: if
\begin{equation}\label{eq:shell-hypotheses}

neither the exceptional set nor its bound involves a choice of $r$.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $U,V$ be finite nonnegative measures, of masses $P,N$.
There are nonnegative submeasures $\mu_+\le U$, $\mu_-\le V$,
both of mass $d=\min(P,N)$, such that
\[
 U-V=\rho+\mu_+-\mu_-,\qquad
 \rho(\R^2)=P-N,\qquad |\rho|(\R^2)=|P-N|.
\]
The residual $\rho$ has constant sign. If $U,V$ are absolutely
continuous and supported in a common closed set, so are all the
constructed measures.

properties.statement_tex:
For every $c\in\mathcal C$ there are measures
$\rho_s^c,\mu_{s,+}^c,\mu_{s,-}^c$ at all vertices
$s\in V_l$, $1\le l\le m$, supported in $\supp\phi_s$ and
absolutely continuous, with $\rho_s^c$ of constant sign and
$\mu_{s,\pm}^c$ nonnegative, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prices-scalar-masses}
 \rho_s^c(\R^2)=c_s,\qquad |\rho_s^c|(\R^2)=|c_s|,
 \qquad
 \mu_{s,+}^c(\R^2)=\mu_{s,-}^c(\R^2)=d_s^c.
\end{equation}
Put $\beta_s^c=\mu_{s,+}^c-\mu_{s,-}^c$. For every
$q\in V_k$, $1\le k\le m$, the following is an identity of
measures on the whole plane:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prices-vertex-reconstruction}
 \phi_q\nu^c=\rho_q^c+
       \sum_{l=k}^m\sum_{s\in V_l}\lambda_{qs}\beta_s^c.
\end{equation}
Only finitely many terms in this identity are nonzero, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prices-pair-properties}
 \beta_s^c(\R^2)=0,\qquad
 |\beta_s^c|(\R^2)\le2d_s^c,\qquad
 \supp\beta_s^c\subseteq\supp\phi_s
       \subseteq\overline B(s,\sqrt2 r_l).
\end{equation}

Let $Q>1$ be odd. Suppose that a finite list of positive integers
$m_1,\ldots,m_t$ satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^t1/m_i=1$ and contains a
multiple of $Q$. Then $1$ has a representation by at most $t$ distinct
positive unit fractions, still with a denominator divisible by $Q$.

\[

 X^{1/2}\le Y\le X,\qquad N\le e^{DS}.
\]

\begin{equation}\label{eq:divisor-moment}
 \sum_{1\le h\le Y}d_X(N+h)^r\le Y\exp(S^{1/4}).

properties.statement_tex:
For every sufficiently large integer $k$,
\[
 \exp\bigl(\exp(k/600)\bigr)\le v(k)\le1+k^{2^{k-1}}.

More precisely,
\[
 \frac{\log2}{257}
 \le\liminf_{k\to\infty}\frac{\log\log v(k)}k
 \le\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\log\log v(k)}k
 \le\log2.
\]
Equivalently for the lower bound, every fixed $c<\log2/257$ satisfies
$v(k)\ge\exp(\exp(ck))$ for every sufficiently large integer $k$.
In particular $\log\log v(k)=\Theta(k)$.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $m\ge4$ and $T\ge2m^2$ be integers.
There are integers $2\le n_1<\cdots<n_j$, none equal to $m$,
and integers $q>0$ and $0\le R<2m$ such that
\[
  1=\frac1m+\sum_{i=1}^{j}\frac1{n_i}+\frac Rq,
  \qquad q=m\prod_{i=1}^{j}n_i,
  \qquad
  j<3+\log_2\log_2 T.
\]
Writing $q_0=m$ and $q_i=m\prod_{h=1}^{i}n_h$ for $1\le i\le j$,
we have $n_i\le q_{i-1}+1$ for every $1\le i\le j$.
If $R>0$, then
\[
  q\ge T,\qquad
  \frac Rq<\frac{2m}{T}\le\frac1m,
  \qquad \frac Rq<\frac1{n_i}\quad(1\le i\le j).
\]
In either case $q<T^2$.

properties.statement_tex:
For every sufficiently large integer $m$, put
\[
 L=\log\log m,\qquad Y=m^4,\qquad
 \ell(v)=\left\lceil\frac{4\log v}{\log 2}\right\rceil
 \quad(v\geq2).
\]
Let $P(v)$ be the product of the first $\ell(v)$ primes, and define
\[
 K_m=P(Y)^2\,\lfloor L\rfloor!.
\]
Then $K_m>m$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:supply-size}
 \log K_m\leq
 \left(\frac{32}{\log 2}+o(1)\right)\log m\log\log m
 \qquad(m\longrightarrow\infty).
\end{equation}
Moreover, every integer $1\leq s\leq Y$ has a representation
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-supply}
 s=\sum_{i=1}^{h}\frac{e_i}{t_i},\qquad
 h\leq16,\quad e_i\mid K_m,\quad e_i,t_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.
\end{equation}
Repeated summands are allowed.

properties.statement_tex:
Let \(K=100\), \(D_0=100000\), and \(m=\lfloor S/\log S\rfloor\).
Let \(\mathcal P\) be a set of primes in \([S^K,2S^K]\) with
\(P=|\mathcal P|\ge S^{K-1}\), and sample
\[
 p_{j,\epsilon}\qquad
 (1\le j\le m,\ \epsilon\in\{0,1\})
\]
independently and uniformly from \(\mathcal P\).  For
\(I\in\{0,1\}^m\), put \(t_I=\prod_{j=1}^m p_{j,I_j}\).
For every integer \(u\) such that
\[
 D_0\log S\le V:=\log u\le S,
 \qquad w=\min(m,V),
\]
and every integer \(1\le l\le \exp(0.005w)\), one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:random-second-moment}
 \E\left|2^{-m}\sum_{I\in\{0,1\}^m}\e(lt_I/u)\right|^2
 \le \exp(-0.01w)
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large \(S\).  The onset is absolute and uniform in
\(u,l,\mathcal P\).

For all sufficiently large \(S\) and every integer \(C\) satisfying
\eqref{eq:C-range}, there are an integer \(M\) and indexed lists
\(T_0,T_1,\ldots,T_R\), each with \(2^m\) entries, such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
\(e^S<M\le e^{D_MS}\), and the least power of \(2\) at least
\(S^{D_0}\) divides \(M\).  Every entry of every \(T_i\) divides \(M\).
\item
For each \(0\le j<d\), let \(T=T_0\) if \(X_j>e^S\), and let
\(T=T_1\) otherwise.  Apart from at most
\(X_j e^{-c_*m}\) integers \(u\in(X_{j+1},X_j]\), at least
\(\rho |T|/2\) entries \(t\in T\) satisfy
\[
 h_{j,t}(u)\le X_{j+1},
 \qquad c_*=0.001.
\]
\item
For every integer \(S^{D_0}<u\le e^m\), some entry \(t\) of one of
\(T_1,\ldots,T_R\) satisfies
\[
 u\lceil t/u\rceil-t\le u^{1-\eta}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Repeated values in a list are counted with their indices.
The threshold on \(S\) is independent of \(C\).

properties.statement: Finite integer n>=1, FULL untruncated bosonic Fock states with finite mean total number. Two ports JOINT PRODUCT rhoA tensor rhoB; arbitrary entanglement WITHIN either port allowed. Same passive transmissivity eta in[0,1] at each mode; reduced retained output. gInv(SC/n)>=eta*gInv(SA/n)+(1-eta)*gInv(SB/n), all natural logs. properties.statement_tex:
Let \(n\ge1\) be finite, and let \(\rho_A,\rho_B\) be states on \(n\) bosonic modes, with annihilation operators \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\) and \(b_1,\ldots,b_n\), respectively, satisfying
\[
 \Tr\rho_A\sum_{j=1}^n a_j^\dagger a_j<\infty,
 \qquad
 \Tr\rho_B\sum_{j=1}^n b_j^\dagger b_j<\infty.
\]
The joint input is \(\rho_A\otimes\rho_B\); no independence assumption is made among the modes within either state. For \(0\le\eta\le1\), let \(\rho_C\) be the reduced state of the modes
\[
 c_j=\sqrt\eta\,a_j+\sqrt{1-\eta}\,b_j,\qquad 1\le j\le n,
\]
after passive beam-splitter mixing. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:epni}
 g^{-1}\!\left(\frac{S(\rho_C)}n\right)
 \ge \eta\,g^{-1}\!\left(\frac{S(\rho_A)}n\right)
 +(1-\eta)\,g^{-1}\!\left(\frac{S(\rho_B)}n\right),
\end{equation}
where \(S(\rho)=-\Tr\rho\log\rho\).

properties.statement_tex:
Let \(\sigma\) be a faithful state, and suppose both \(S(\rho)\) and \(\Tr\rho(-\log\sigma)\) are finite. Then
\[

\]
with equality if and only if \(\rho=\sigma\).
Consequently, if \(K\) is bounded below and \(0<Z=\Tr e^{-K}<\infty\), its Gibbs state \(Z^{-1}e^{-K}\) uniquely minimizes \(\Tr\rho K-S(\rho)\) among states for which these expressions are finite, provided that Gibbs state belongs to the admitted class.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $b:[0,\infty)\times\R^I\longrightarrow[0,1]^I$ be jointly Borel.
Suppose that a constant $0\le L<\infty$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-lipschitz}
 \sup_{i\in I}|b_i(t,y)-b_i(t,y')|
 \le L\sup_{j\in I}|y_j-y'_j|
\end{equation}
for every $t\ge0$ and every $y,y'\in\R^I$ whose coordinate differences
have finite supremum.  Then, for every $w\in\mathcal C_I$, there is a
unique $Z(w)\in\mathcal C_I$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:inverse-equation}
 Z_i(w)(t)=w_i(t)+\int_0^t b_i(s,Z(w)(s))\,ds,
 \qquad i\in I,\quad t\ge0.
\end{equation}
The map $Z:\mathcal C_I\longrightarrow\mathcal C_I$ is Borel and
causal: its restriction to $[0,T]$ depends only on the input restricted
to $[0,T]$.  It commutes with every coordinate relabeling under which
the drift is equivariant.

Let $\nu$ be a probability law on $\{0,1\}^I$, where $I$ is countable,
and for each $i$ choose finite sets $S_n(i)$ increasing to $I$.
Interpret the finite-tilt functions \eqref{eq:finite-tilt} and the
limsup drift \eqref{eq:drift} with this law and these sets.
Suppose that the finite-tilt functions $b_{i,S_n(i)}(t,\cdot)$ are
$L$-Lipschitz in the supremum norm on their finite fields, with one
constant $0\le L<\infty$ for all $i,n$ and $t\ge0$.
Then the drift has the Borel solution map of Lemma~\ref{lem:inverse},
and the Borel map $\Psi:\mathcal C_I\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^I$
defined by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:readout}
 \Psi_i(w)=
 \1\left\{\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{Z_i(w)(n)}{n}>\frac12\right\}
\end{equation}
sends the law of independent standard Brownian paths to $\nu$.
The map $\Psi$ inherits every coordinate relabeling equivariance of
the drift.

properties.statement_tex:
Let $F$ be a nonempty finite set and let $\mu$ be a strongly Rayleigh
probability law on $\{0,1\}^F$. For $h\in\R^F$, let
\[
 \mu_h(x)=\frac{\exp(\sum_{j\in F}h_jx_j)\mu(x)}
 {\sum_{z\in\{0,1\}^F}\exp(\sum_{j\in F}h_jz_j)\mu(z)},
 \qquad p_i(h)=\E_{\mu_h}X_i.
\]
For every $i,j\in F$, the derivative identity below holds, and for every
$i\in F$ the row satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sr-covariance-row}
 \frac{\partial p_i}{\partial h_j}
 =\Cov_{\mu_h}(X_i,X_j),
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\in F}\left|\frac{\partial p_i}{\partial h_j}\right|
 \le 2p_i(h)(1-p_i(h))\le\frac12.
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sr-response}
 |p_i(h)-p_i(h')|\le\frac12\max_{j\in F}|h_j-h'_j|
 \qquad(h,h'\in\R^F).
\end{equation}

properties.statement_tex:
Given $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\ell_1$, either all the points coincide,
or there exist a finite set $\mathcal B$, positive weights
$(w_B)_{B\in\mathcal B}$, binary vectors
$z_i\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal B}$, and an affine map
$T:\R^{\mathcal B}\to\ell_1$ with the following properties.
For
\[
 \|u\|_{1,w}=\sum_{B\in\mathcal B}w_B|u_B|,
 \qquad
 \|u\|_H^2=\sum_{B\in\mathcal B}w_Bu_B^2,
\]
one has
\begin{align}
 T(z_i)&=x_i,\label{eq:reconstruct}\\
 \|x_i-x_j\|_1
 &=\|z_i-z_j\|_{1,w}=\|z_i-z_j\|_H^2,
 \label{eq:cut-distance}\\
 \|T(u)-T(u')\|_1&\leq\|u-u'\|_{1,w}
 \qquad(u,u'\in\R^{\mathcal B}).\label{eq:contraction}
\end{align}
The space $H$ is $\R^{\mathcal B}$ with the indicated Hilbert norm.
